articleTitle: Overview and Recent Progress on the Development of Compact GaN-based Power Converters
publicationTitle: Power Electronic Components and their Applications 2017; 7. ETG-Symposium
abstract: This paper is devoted to the recent advances of compact high-density Gallium-Nitride (GaN)-based power converters and related technologies. GaN-based diodes, and both lateral and new vertical devices are discussed. Vertical devices are recently becoming available while the reliability of lateral devices is improving, and test methods and degradation mechanisms are becoming better understood. Aspects of compact monolithic and heterogenous integration are being discussed.

articleTitle: Modularity of Grid Inverters in Modern Power Systems
publicationTitle: Power Electronic Components and their Applications 2017; 7. ETG-Symposium
abstract: This work discusses the benefits of a modular scheme for grid inverters of various components of modern power systems. The grid applications considered in this work are wind turbines, battery packs and static synchronous compensators (STATCOM). The grid connecting scheme is based on the parallel connection of several inverter-modules. The advantages of such a concept as far as reliability, costoptimization and grid behavior are in detail presented. Field measurements of a wind turbine validate the optimal grid behavior of the modular topology.

articleTitle: Last Advances in Electrolytic and Film Capacitors for Power Electronics
publicationTitle: Power Electronic Components and their Applications 2017; 7. ETG-Symposium
abstract: The requirements for passive components in power electronics are mainly ruled by the capabilities of the semiconductor technology [1]. The evolution into faster devices, with higher current handling, voltage ratings and operation temperature is a reality with the upcoming SiC and GaN technology. Semiconductor devices based on SiC are also able to switch ten times faster than the equivalent silicon based semiconductors [2-4]. As a direct consequence, capacitors designed to work in SiC based converters will be required to have high current density capability, and very low and homogeneously distributed inductance. Another advantage of SiC semiconductors is that they can operate at up to 400 deg C and they have three times higher thermal conductivity as Si semiconductors [2]. In order to take complete advantage of the high operation temperature it is as well desirable that the maximum allowable temperature on the passive components, specifically the capacitors, has to be increased. In general, due to the evolution of the semiconductors in the last years and a qualitative step forward coming up with the wide-bandgap semiconductor technology the power capacitors are required to have more compact and cheap designs, with high energy density and current handling capability and able to operate at high frequencies. The resulting heat generation and operating conditions should be carefully studied in the design-in phase. In this article, relevant design considerations on the equivalent series resistance and inductivity in aluminum electrolytic and film capacitors that have major impact in the long term reliability and lifetime are discussed.

articleTitle: Modular Multilevel Converter - Impact on future applications and semiconductors
publicationTitle: Power Electronic Components and their Applications 2017; 7. ETG-Symposium
abstract: Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) has opened new roads for power electronics. Starting with the basic structure and functionality of MMC, new requirements and options for future advanced converters are described. An analysis of development trends of the power semiconductors reveals, that combinations of silicon and silicon carbide devices offer great potentials for essential improvements in the next decade.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Power Devices as Key Technology for a Future Sustainable Society
publicationTitle: Power Electronic Components and their Applications 2017; 7. ETG-Symposium
abstract: Power Electronics is a key technology for sustainable traffic, for efficient information technology, for renewable energy supply, for automatization and for energy efficiency. It is the interface between computing and action. Long-time technical trends to an "intelligent electrified society" give the expectation for a high growth of more than a factor of ten in the next two decades. Wide bandgap devices compete with silicon devices with the IGBT as key element. A large progress with the Si based IGBT is still possible. There is no replacement to be expected; it is more likely that a strong growth in all fields with space for even new technologies will take place. Packaging, reliability and system integration are essential features.

articleTitle: Recent Achievements and Future Development Trends of High Voltage Si-based Devices
publicationTitle: Power Electronic Components and their Applications 2017; 7. ETG-Symposium
abstract: This paper gives an overview of the latest achievements in the area of Si-based turn-off devices for high voltage applications in the power range beyond 10MW. Today, two device technologies are available in this power range depending on the application demands: The Integrated Gate Commutated Thyristor (IGCT) and the Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT). In this paper, we will show the latest development trends of these two devices, including some relevant packaging results.

articleTitle: Power Electronics for the Light of the Future
publicationTitle: Power Electronic Components and their Applications 2017; 7. ETG-Symposium
abstract: When state-of-the-art LED lighting is connected and managed through smart controls in the Internet of Things, the lighting experience is improved while electricity demand can be reduced. Many aspects of LED drivers used for current LED technology (LEDification) are well established. Of these, this paper reviews offline LED drivers and compatibility with installed control gear. Smart LED drivers used for connected lighting pose new challenges which remain to be explored.
